scope: Proposition 9.2 (Calibrated renewal inputs) of the manuscript “Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints” (preprints/Critical-honeycomb-chords-with-prescribed-boundary-endpoints-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b7adfc0aa278ae3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the port-rooted irreducible law, write Y, Z, L, D for integral height, lateral displacement, length and diameter. Then 2Z is integral, Pr(D > r) ≤ Cr−3/4, 1 − Ee−tY ≍ t3/4, and 1 − Ee−tL = t9/16+o(1). In addition: (i) For k independent whole pieces, supj Pr(SY (k) = j) ≤ Ck−4/3 and supw Pr(S(Y,Z)(k) = w) ≤ Ck−8/3. The off-axis bridge construction gives positive mass in directional windows; all atoms use the actual lattice. (ii) Start two independent sequences at the same bottom port through the same first center v. Retain completed pieces at heights strictly below s, excluding the first piece reaching or passing s. Fix left and right roles. At every pair of renewal levels 0 < d1 < d2 < s from the left and right histories respectively, require that the prefixes be disjoint after v, leave on opposite sides of v, and that every right-prefix crossing at d1 lie strictly right of the left terminal coordinate. The probability of all these requirements is at most Cη(1 + s)−3/4+η for each η > 0. At a shared turn this applies with s = 1 vacuously, or with s sufficiently below both adjacent arm heights that distant endpoint adjustments do not affect the tests. For the two arms used below, extending both to the same top port duplicates just their highest center. The resulting factor of κ is absorbed by an absolute constant; no shape-dependent trimming is used in this application. (iii) For every sufficiently small fixed ξ > 0, some c, C > 0 give the absolute critical mass estimate X ω rooted at a fixed center R≤diam ω≤2R, L(ω)≤R4/3−ξ κL(ω) ≤ Ce−Rc .
